issues.legal_issue: A contention based on a statutory restriction cannot be introduced for the first time at a later stage of review when no foundation for it was laid in the pleadings or earlier proceedings.
material_facts: The landowner relied on a statutory limit on the tenant’s purchase rights for the first time before the High Court.
The landowner had not pleaded facts relevant to that limit or raised the contention before the revenue authorities.
The landowner had also pursued claims concerning other tenants but did not continue those claims after the tribunal’s decisions.
issues.conclusion: The landowner was not entitled to raise the contention because no foundation for it had been laid in the pleadings or at any earlier stage.
issues.legal_principle: A party cannot raise a contention at a later stage when the pleadings and earlier proceedings contain no factual foundation for it. The Court did not decide the scope or meaning of section 42(c) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Land (Vidharbha and Kutch Area) Act, 1958, and relied on no earlier cases for this ruling.

predicates.appellate_proceeding: The dispute was before a court reviewing decisions made in earlier proceedings.
predicates.contention_omitted_from_pleadings: The party had not pleaded facts supporting the contention.
predicates.contention_not_raised_earlier: The party had not raised the contention before the earlier decision-makers.
predicates.late_raised_contention_barred: The party cannot raise the contention at the later stage.

issues.definition: When a party in a reviewing proceeding omitted a contention from the pleadings and did not raise it earlier, the contention is barred at the later stage.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s statutory ownership of eligible tenanted land vests automatically on the prescribed date, and a later amendment deeming a failure to purchase to be a surrender does not undo that vesting.
material_facts: The tenant held the disputed land as a protected lessee and did not take steps to purchase it.

The applicable law provided for ownership of eligible tenanted land to vest in the tenant from a date earlier than the amendment that added a deemed-surrender consequence for failure to exercise the purchase right.
No proceeding to terminate the tenancy was pending on the vesting date.
issues.conclusion: The tenant became the statutory owner of the land on the vesting date despite not taking steps to purchase it; the later amendment did not operate retrospectively to affect that ownership.
issues.legal_principle: Section 46(1) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Land (Vidharbha and Kutch Area) Act, 1958 provided for ownership of land eligible for purchase under Chapter III to vest in the tenant from the prescribed date. Section 41 provided the purchase right, and section 43(14A), inserted later, deemed land surrendered when a tenant failed to exercise that right. The later insertion did not operate retrospectively and could not displace ownership already vested under section 46(1). The Court relied on no earlier cases for this ruling.

rule.if: tenancy_ownership_dispute and land_eligible_for_tenant_purchase and statute_provided_automatic_vesting and vesting_preceded_later_surrender_amendment

predicates.tenancy_ownership_dispute: The dispute concerned whether a tenant acquired ownership of land held under a tenancy.
predicates.land_eligible_for_tenant_purchase: The land held by the tenant was land the tenant was entitled to purchase under the applicable tenancy scheme.
predicates.statute_provided_automatic_vesting: The applicable law provided that ownership of eligible tenanted land would vest in the tenant automatically from a prescribed date.
predicates.vesting_preceded_later_surrender_amendme: The prescribed vesting date came before a later amendment that treated failure to exercise a purchase right as a surrender.
predicates.tenant_ownership_vested_automatically: The tenant acquired statutory ownership of the eligible land from the prescribed vesting date.

issues.definition: When a tenancy ownership dispute concerns land eligible for purchase, the law provides for automatic vesting, and that vesting predates a later surrender amendment, ownership vests automatically in the tenant.
